about: The top four of five concepts after three judged rounds (6 Nov), in the order the judging handed them over, best first: a Untangle 38, b Exploded View 38, c Taken Apart 37, d Prism 38 (kept as handed over: Taken Apart's 37 sits above Prism's 38 in that order; the reason was not given). scores = the judge's final score for each of the 21 bet questions, in bet.json order (b1.f, b1.e, b1.i, b2.f ... b7.i), 0/1/2. sections = each section's number, title and the bet questions it answers (the concept's own claim). notes = the judge's round-3 notes, shortened. Ours, not the client's.

options.name: Untangle
options.premise: EWC had a heap of value it couldn't break down. The page hands the reader that heap, lets them sort it (or watch it sort), shows how we sorted it (who it's for, what they come for, what they'd do otherwise), and ends by asking how the reader would have done it.

sections.title: Title, the four things, the tag
The tangle, and the two voices at work
One piece of evidence: a Tuesday
The wrong member, and the right one

options.notes: Spine is right: value broken down, Tuesday held to one section, no timeline; more of Kahran's own lines on the page than any other. Fixes it asks for: too many devices (sort, side by side, auto-playing dominoes, a door whose light runs into a seat); the four-labels row reads as case-study nav, keep it as what Joyus makes and give 'more from EWC' its own link; mark the bar counts 'our count' and reconcile home; the persona names are Joyus's writing; the home-page line sits outside 46-50; b4.i half done, the quote slot is empty.

options.name: Exploded View
options.premise: EWC had one solid value they couldn't take apart. The page is one exploded-view drawing of it: the block comes apart into who it's for, what each comes for, what it replaces and what the club gives them, then goes back together with its seams showing. The seams are what Joyus made.

sections.title: Cut two: what each one comes for
Would you have cut it there?

options.notes: Strongest single metaphor for value they couldn't break down; his list as four machined faces is the best b1.f on the table; the Tuesday held to one inset. Fixes it asks for: too much machinery (scrubber, 24 tiles, 14 trays, dominoes, tick, a drawing tool, a field); the persona names and gives are Joyus's writing set upright; the block's live line sits outside 46-50; b4.i still a pending bracket (a founder line exists, flagged, not used); keep his 'who you target... who you attract' wording.

options.name: Taken Apart
options.premise: The club's value arrives as one solid, undivided bar. Our italic hand cuts it, the way an editor marks up a page, into what members come for, who it's for, and with what. Nothing explains the meta-analysis; you see it in the cuts. It asks where you'd cut before we do, then hands you the knife.

sections.title: What they come for, who it's for, with what (the hero)
What they'd do otherwise (the one Tuesday section)

options.notes: The best visual discipline: one editor's-markup metaphor, the wiring diagram as a true hero, about a dozen short italic lines, two pen hands as the two-person team; the stet on the leagues line is the one tender moment any concept earned. Fixes it asks for: his 'the problem solved, and the members they wanted' was missing at the seats (put back here); the four brackets are forced; the lump is the guide's gives, which we wrote, so 'every word here is theirs' was untrue (changed here); the home-page line sits outside 46-50; §6 is three mechanics; b4.i quote slot empty.

options.name: Prism
options.premise: EWC had value they couldn't break down: one grey slab holding everything on offer. The page passes it through a prism and it splits into six coloured beams, one per member, each carrying what that member comes for. It asks how the reader would split it, shows how we did, and asks again.

sections.title: The slab, the question, the tag
The cost of the wrong member

options.notes: The title is his framing word for word; the prism facets carry his b1.f list; the six beams read in a glance; the Tuesday is a postage stamp. Fixes it asks for: the slab is built from the guide's per-member gives, which we wrote, so it is labelled here 'everything on offer, pooled', not 'what the club said to everyone'; low-contrast text as texture is still words standing in for a visual; b4.i is two empty frames (here: the home page, circled; the quote slot hidden); one tag format (aligned here); §5 carries too much.
